hero.title: Howdy hey!
hero.body: I’m Nyuu, a computer science student passionate about learning new things every day. I run managed hosting and set up Linux, Docker and Kubernetes infrastructure.
hero.personaAlt: Nyuu, a cat-eared character in a black hat, tipping it with a wink

services.title: Services
services.note: What I can do for you

hosting.title: Managed hosting
hosting.lead: Reliable, hassle-free hosting where everything is taken care of for you.
hosting.detail: Enjoy smooth, worry-free hosting with full management included. I handle server setup, updates, security, and monitoring so your apps and websites run at their best, whether it’s on bare metal, virtualized environments, or cloud platforms. You’ll have the performance and stability you need without the stress of maintenance.

setup.title: Installation & setup
setup.lead: Get your infrastructure up and running the right way, from the start.
setup.detail: From Linux servers to Docker stacks and Kubernetes clusters, I make sure everything is properly installed, configured, and ready to go. Whether you’re setting up a new environment or migrating an existing one, I ensure each component works together seamlessly: secure, stable, and optimized for your needs.

backups.title: Backups & recovery
backups.lead: Keep your data safe with reliable backup and recovery solutions.
backups.detail: I design and deploy backup strategies that protect your data from loss, downtime, or disasters. Using automated tools and best practices, I ensure your files, databases, and configurations are securely stored and can be restored quickly when needed, giving you peace of mind and business continuity.

custom.title: Custom solutions
custom.lead: Tailored solutions built around your specific goals and infrastructure.
custom.detail: Every project is unique, and sometimes off-the-shelf tools aren’t enough. I create customized setups and automations to fit your workflow, from Dockerized apps and cloud integrations to monitoring dashboards or storage backends. Whatever your challenge, I’ll help you design a solution that’s efficient, scalable, and easy to manage.

whiskers.description: Open models for coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and any OpenAI SDK connect through one OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API. One payment buys several times its price in official API usage, and nothing renews on its own.
whiskers.lead: Whiskers sells open models to coding agents. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and anything with an OpenAI SDK connect to one API that speaks OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s formats. A plan is one payment for a set number of days that buys several times its price in official API usage, and nothing renews on its own.
whiskers.featuresNote: For the people who code with it, and for running it.

agents.title: Every coding agent
agents.text: Claude Code speaks Anthropic’s Messages API, Codex OpenAI’s Responses API, and OpenCode, Crush, Aider, pi, Cline, Zed and the rest chat completions. One setup command configures six of them, keeping the config already there.

payment.title: One payment, no auto-renew
payment.text: A plan runs for its days from payment and then ends: nothing carries over and nothing is charged. Prepaid credits cover requests directly and never expire. Checkout runs on Stripe or Mercado Pago.

windows.title: Three windows, one allowance
windows.text: A 5-hour, a weekly and a monthly window are three views of the same allowance, so one busy afternoon can’t use up the month. A request runs when every window can cover it.

value.title: Priced against the official APIs
value.text: Every offer shows what its credits would cost at the model publishers’ own API prices, and the console shows what each request actually cost.

docs.title: Docs for people and agents
docs.text: The landing page and the docs are prerendered in English and Portuguese, as HTML for search engines and link previews and as Markdown for agents. Each agent’s guide is built from the live catalog.

operations.title: Run from one console
operations.text: Admins onboard providers and models with health checks and a circuit breaker, and handle coupons, referrals, support tickets and site-wide announcements.

built: The backend is a modular monolith on Python 3.13, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 and PostgreSQL, its only required infrastructure. One image runs as two processes: the API, which serves every HTTP surface and streams responses as they arrive, and a worker for the sweeper, usage rollups, payment webhooks and reconciliation. Each module exposes a single public interface, and import contracts keep the boundaries.

The dashboard is React 19 and TypeScript on Vite, with TanStack Router and Query and Tailwind, in the Ledger design this site shares. Its API types are generated from the backend’s OpenAPI schema and checked against it.

syncr.description: A self-hosted manager for rclone transfers and restic backups. One controller with a web UI drives workers on Linux and Windows: run jobs by hand or on a schedule, follow them live, browse and restore snapshots, and get notified when something fails.
syncr.lead: Syncr manages rclone transfers and restic backups from one place. A controller with a web UI drives any number of workers on your servers and desktops, Linux or Windows: run jobs by hand or on a schedule, watch them live, browse files and snapshots, and get notified when something fails.
syncr.featuresNote: Transfers, backups and the machines that run them, from one web UI.

transfers.title: rclone transfers
transfers.text: Copy, sync or move between S3 and compatibles, SFTP, Backblaze B2, WebDAV and a worker’s own folders, with live progress, speed and time left. Two-way sync keeps a folder in step on several machines, and stops a run that would empty a side.

backups.title: restic backups
backups.text: Create or connect repositories on any remote, back up a worker’s folders or a folder of a remote, and apply retention. Browse snapshots, restore all of one or selected files, search every snapshot for a file, and compare two.

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.text: Cron expressions with time zones and daylight-saving rules, run on one worker or on the least busy one with a label, with policies for missed runs and overlaps.

workers.title: Workers anywhere
workers.text: Workers run as services on Linux and Windows, connect to the controller or let it connect to them over pinned TLS, and upgrade in place with automatic rollback.

notify.title: Hooks and notifications
notify.text: Run a worker’s prepared commands before and after a job, such as dumping a database or stopping containers. Discord, email and signed webhooks are stored before sending and retried.

security.title: Secure and multi-user
security.text: Credentials are encrypted at rest and sent only to the worker that runs the job, which can only touch the folders it allows. Accounts keep their remotes and schedules private, with personal API tokens for everything the UI does.

built: Syncr 2 is a Go rewrite of the first version, which was built on Django. One controller keeps its state in PostgreSQL, serves a Connect API, and embeds the React and TypeScript UI; workers run pinned versions of rclone and restic as child processes and report progress as they go.

The code follows ports and adapters, with the layers enforced by the linter, so the use cases never touch PostgreSQL or the network directly. CI runs on Linux and Windows, with integration tests against real PostgreSQL, MinIO and SFTP, and the controller ships as a Docker image or a single binary.
